scenes.heading: Factorising non-monic quadratics
scenes.sub: A method that never needs guessing
scenes.say: What do you do when there's a number in front of x squared, like three x squared minus ten x minus eight? Guessing brackets is slow. In this video you'll learn a method that works every time.
scenes.caption: What do you do when there's a number in front of x², like 3x² − 10x − 8? Guessing brackets is slow. In this video you'll learn a method that works every time.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Four players split into two pairs, and both pairs wear the same jersey
scenes.science: Split into 4 terms, group in pairs, take out the shared bracket
scenes.breaks: Players can pair up any way, but brackets only match if you split using the right numbers.
scenes.say: Picture four players split into two pairs, both wearing the same team jersey. Then you can say two groups of that team. Splitting the middle term turns three terms into four. Grouping them in pairs makes the same bracket, the jersey, appear twice, so you can take it out.

scenes.heading: The ac method
steps: Find numbers: multiply to ac, add to b
Group in pairs, take out the bracket
scenes.say: Here's the method. First take out any common factor. Then multiply a times c, and find two numbers that multiply to a c and add to b. Use them to split the middle term. Finally, group in pairs and take out the common bracket.

scenes.heading: Why a × c?
scenes.say: Here is two x squared plus seven x plus three as a rectangle. First the outline, then the sides two x plus one and x plus three, then the four parts. The two diagonal parts multiply to six x squared, and so do the two strips. So the strips come from numbers that multiply to a times c, six, and add to seven.
scenes.caption: 2x² + 7x + 3 as a rectangle with sides 2x + 1 and x + 3. The diagonal parts multiply to 6x², and so do the strips x and 6x. So the strips come from numbers that multiply to ac = 6 and add to 7.

scenes.heading: Worked example
scenes.question: Factorise 3x² − 10x − 8.
scenes.say: Factorise three x squared minus ten x minus eight. a times c is negative twenty-four. Negative twelve and two multiply to that and add to negative ten. Split the middle term, then group. Both pairs share x minus four, so the answer is x minus four, times three x plus two.
scenes.caption: Factorise 3x² − 10x − 8. ac = −24; −12 and 2 multiply to −24 and add to −10. Split, then group. Both pairs share (x − 4): (x − 4)(3x + 2).

scenes.heading: Matching the brackets
scenes.question: Factorise 6x² − 11x + 4.
scenes.say: Six x squared minus eleven x plus four. a c is twenty-four, and negative three and negative eight add to negative eleven. When you group, take out negative four from the second pair so its bracket matches: two x minus one. The answer is two x minus one, times three x minus four.
scenes.caption: 6x² − 11x + 4. ac = 24; −3 and −8 add to −11. Take out −4 from the second pair so the brackets match: (2x − 1)(3x − 4).

points: Multiply to ac, add to b
Split, group, pull out the bracket
scenes.say: Quick recap. Take out any common factor first. Find two numbers that multiply to a c and add to b. Split, group, and pull out the matching bracket. If the brackets don't match, check your signs, and always expand to check. Now try the practice questions!
